issue.title: Update: XSS_Filter_Evasion_Cheat_Sheet
issue.body:
## What is missing or needs to be updated?

The XSS Filter Evasion Cheat Sheet is 1,143 lines. Many of its vectors depend on legacy engines. The sheet refers to IE 16 times (VBScript, HTC files, XML data islands, CSS expressions), and it also has Gecko-only tricks like `-moz-binding` and META `Set-Cookie`, which modern browsers ignore.

Some entries are not XSS filter evasion at all: SSI and PHP are server-side execution, and "IMG Embedded Commands" is really CSRF. The BODY event-handler list is about 135 lines and mixes standard events with IE-only ones like `onBounce`.

## How should this be resolved?

- Separate legacy-engine vectors from tests that matter for modern browsers. Edge IE mode still runs Trident for some intranet apps, so IE-only vectors can move into one short legacy section rather than disappear entirely.
- Remove vectors that only worked in engines nobody tests anymore.
- Trim the BODY event-handler list to standard events.
- Drop the entries that aren't XSS filter evasion (SSI, PHP, IMG Embedded Commands).
- Fix the alert-obfuscation examples that use curly quotes.
- Each removal or legacy move should say which browser or engine the vector depended on, so reviewers can check it.

Small PRs, one section at a time, please. They are much easier to review than one big rewrite :)

2877.title: docs: propose migration of IMG CSRF examples out of XSS guide
2877.body:
## Summary

This PR migrates the two historical `IMG Embedded Commands` examples out of the XSS Filter Evasion Cheat Sheet into a proposed **Browser-Initiated Request Abuse Cheat Sheet**, addressing the maintainer's feedback on #2792.

The new document preserves both request patterns while correcting outdated technical claims and explaining the relevant browser and session limitations.

## Changes

- Removed the two non-XSS sections from `cheatsheets/XSS_Filter_Evasion_Cheat_Sheet.md`.
- Added `cheatsheets/Browser_Initiated_Request_Abuse_Cheat_Sheet.md`, documenting direct image requests and image requests followed by HTTP redirects.
- Updated `Index.md` to include the new guide.
- Preserved the historical attribution to Timo.

## Technical Accuracy

- Clarified that `302 Found` supports redirection, whereas `304 Not Modified` is related to cache validation.
- Explained the role of session credentials, SameSite cookies, authorization, and CSRF protection.
- Used illustrative `.test` URLs rather than operational targets.
- Avoided classifying these patterns as XSS execution or proven WAF bypass.

## Validation

- [x] Reviewed the three-file diff.
- [x] Verified the migration of both examples.
- [x] Performed basic Markdown structure and citation checks.
- [ ] Awaiting GitHub Actions approval and successful CI execution.
- [ ] Awaiting maintainer approval of the new cheat sheet's title and scope.

## References

- [OWASP CSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross-Site_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html)
- [RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html)
- [MDN — Set-Cookie](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Set-Cookie)

## AI Tool Usage Disclosure

- [ ] I have NOT used AI tools to generate the contents of this PR.
- [x] I have used AI tools to prepare and review this contribution.

**Tool:** ChatGPT (GPT-6).

**Usage:** AI-assisted research, technical analysis, drafting of the new cheat sheet, and review. The contribution remains subject to maintainer verification.

**Prompt summary:** Review issue #2792, PR #2877, the existing documentation and contribution guidelines; migrate the two examples into a correctly scoped security guide; verify primary HTTP/CSRF references; and update the documentation index.

The contribution was reviewed for accuracy, scope, and consistency with the cited sources. No Codex was used.

## Scope and Approval

This contribution addresses the migration requested in #2792 while leaving the remaining cleanup tasks outside the scope of this PR.

The proposed new cheat sheet's title, scope, and destination remain subject to maintainer approval under the project's contribution guidelines.

**New cheat sheet proposal:** #2887

The original issue should remain open for the remaining cleanup tasks.

2892.title: docs(xss): drop server-side execution sections and fix alert quotes (#2792)
2892.body:
## Summary

This focused PR addresses part of the cleanup requested in #2792 by @jmanico on the XSS Filter Evasion Cheat Sheet:

1. **Drop non-XSS server-side execution sections:** Removed the `SSI (Server Side Includes)` and `PHP` sections. As noted in the tracking issue, SSI (`<!--#exec cmd=...``) and PHP (`<? echo(...)``) represent server-side command/script execution rather than client-side XSS filter evasion.
2. **Normalize curly quotes:** Replaced right double quotation mark (`”`) and right single quotation mark (`’`) with standard ASCII quotes (`"` and `'`) in the `Filter Bypass Alert Obfuscation` payload line and fixed curly apostrophe (`’`) in the Stored XSS section to prevent copy-paste execution failures in testing consoles.

## Scope and sourcing

- [x] This PR is focused: it modifies a single cheat sheet (`cheatsheets/XSS_Filter_Evasion_Cheat_Sheet.md`).
- [x] Tested locally with `markdownlint` with zero lint errors.
- [x] Does not add new unverified claims.

This PR addresses #2792.

## AI Tool Usage Disclosure

- [x] I have NOT used any AI tool to generate the contents of this PR.

2918.title: docs(xss): normalize quotes and apostrophe in WAF bypass strings (#2792)
2918.body:
## Summary

Following maintainer @mackowski's guidance on #2792:
- Replaced curly right double quote (`”`) and right single quote (`’`) in the WAF bypass payload (line 1085) with standard ASCII quotes (`"` and `'`) to prevent syntax/execution failures when testing in consoles.
- Normalized the curly apostrophe in "wouldn’t" to ASCII single quote (`wouldn't`) in the Stored XSS section (line 1017).

As requested by the maintainer, this PR is strictly scoped to only these two lines.

## Scope and sourcing

- [x] This PR is focused: it modifies a single cheat sheet, or a small coordinated set, and the scope is described in the PR body.
- [x] Every technical claim, recommendation, or threat assertion added in this PR is supported by a primary source (RFC, NIST, OWASP standard, vendor documentation, peer-reviewed research) linked inline as `[text](URL)`.
- [x] I have read each source I cite and confirm it actually supports the claim. I have not relied on summaries, hearsay, or model-generated citations.

This PR fixes issue #2792.
